## Description {#details}

<p>Internal implementation details for the µTest++ framework.</p>


<p>The <span class="doxyComputerOutput"><a href="/micro-test-plus-xpack/docs/api/namespaces/micro-os-plus/micro-test-plus/detail">detail</a></span> namespace encapsulates the internal mechanisms, helper structures, and implementation utilities employed by the µTest++ testing framework. These components do not form part of the public API and may be modified without prior notice.</p>


<p>Within this namespace, one will find the deprecated value wrappers (declared in <span class="doxyComputerOutput"><a href="/micro-test-plus-xpack/docs/api/files/include/micro-os-plus/micro-test-plus/deprecated-h">deprecated.h</a></span>), the value unwrapping helper, comparator structures for logical and relational operations, mechanisms for exception checking, the reporters, the check result, and the expression formatter.</p>


<p>All definitions within <span class="doxyComputerOutput"><a href="/micro-test-plus-xpack/docs/api/namespaces/micro-os-plus/micro-test-plus/detail">detail</a></span> are intended exclusively for internal use; the applications do not need to name them.</p>

</table>
</div>
<div class="doxyMemberDoc">

<p>The type with which an expression stores an operand.</p>


<p>Applied by the deduction guides and the factory functions to the type deduced for a forwarding reference: <span class="doxyComputerOutput">X&amp;</span> (or <span class="doxyComputerOutput">const X&amp;</span>) for an lvalue, <span class="doxyComputerOutput">X</span> for an rvalue.</p>


<p>An lvalue is copied into the expression, so that an expression built in a function from its parameters, and returned, does not refer to the destroyed locals of that function. An rvalue is moved into the expression, so that an expression that outlives the statement, like <span class="doxyComputerOutput">auto <a href="/micro-test-plus-xpack/docs/api/structs/micro-os-plus/micro-test-plus/detail/op">op</a> = <a href="/micro-test-plus-xpack/docs/api/groups/micro-os-plus-micro-test-plus-cpp-api-function-comparators/#ga0fbc0f7ddf0107c1e5265bb79287487d">eq</a> (f (), 1);</span>, does not refer to a destroyed temporary.</p>


<p>The arrays and the character pointers are first converted by <span class="doxyComputerOutput"><a href="#a51e86043001b197561806d5c6297041b">as_operand()</a></span> to <span class="doxyComputerOutput"><a href="/micro-test-plus-xpack/docs/api/structs/micro-os-plus/micro-test-plus/detail/basic-c-string">basic_c_string</a></span> or <span class="doxyComputerOutput"><a href="/micro-test-plus-xpack/docs/api/structs/micro-os-plus/micro-test-plus/detail/array-operand">array_operand</a></span>, which are stored, but which refer to the characters or to the elements of the operand, without copying them; such an expression is valid only as long as the operand.</p>


<p>Only an lvalue of a class type that cannot be copied (for example a <span class="doxyComputerOutput">std::unique_ptr</span>) is stored as a <span class="doxyComputerOutput">const</span> reference; such a reference remains valid only as long as the named operand, which is always the case within the statement that checks the expression.</p>

<div class="doxyMemberDoc">

<p>Appends the shortest decimal representation of a numeric value to a buffer.</p>


<dl class="doxyParamsList">
<dt class="doxyParamsTableTitle">Template Parameters</dt>
<dd>
<table class="doxyParamsTable">
<tr class="doxyParamItem">
<td class="doxyParamItemName">T</td>
<td class="doxyParamItemDescription"><p>The numeric type to format.</p></td>
</tr>
</table>
</dd>
</dl>

<dl class="doxyParamsList">
<dt class="doxyParamsTableTitle">Parameters</dt>
<dd>
<table class="doxyParamsTable">
<tr class="doxyParamItem">
<td class="doxyParamItemName">buffer</td>
<td class="doxyParamItemDescription"><p>The string to append to.</p></td>
</tr>
<tr class="doxyParamItem">
<td class="doxyParamItemName">v</td>
<td class="doxyParamItemDescription"><p>The value to format.</p></td>
</tr>
</table>
</dd>

<dl class="doxySectionUser">
<dt>Returns</dt>
<dd><p>Nothing.</p></dd>
</dl>


<p>The value is formatted into a local buffer, which is then appended to <span class="doxyComputerOutput">buffer</span>.</p>


<p>For <span class="doxyComputerOutput">long double</span>, a platform-specific path is chosen:</p>


<ul class="doxyList ">
<li>On Windows and on platforms where <span class="doxyComputerOutput">long double</span> has the same storage width as <span class="doxyComputerOutput">double</span> (e.g. 32-bit Arm), the value is cast to <span class="doxyComputerOutput">double</span> and formatted with <span class="doxyComputerOutput">std::to_chars</span>.</li>
<li>On all other platforms (e.g. x86-64 Linux/macOS with 80-bit extended precision, or AArch64 and RISC-V with 128-bit quad precision), <span class="doxyComputerOutput">snprintf</span> with <span class="doxyComputerOutput">%.*Lg</span> is used as a portable fallback, because <span class="doxyComputerOutput">std::to_chars</span> for <span class="doxyComputerOutput">long double</span> may be unavailable (e.g. when linking with <span class="doxyComputerOutput">lld</span>). The precision starts at <span class="doxyComputerOutput">LDBL_DIG</span> and is increased until the text reads back, with <span class="doxyComputerOutput">strtold</span>, as the same value, up to <span class="doxyComputerOutput">LDBL_DECIMAL_DIG</span>, which always reads back exactly. This gives the shortest exact form, as <span class="doxyComputerOutput">std::to_chars</span> gives for the other types; a shorter form would need fewer than <span class="doxyComputerOutput">LDBL_DIG</span> digits, and <span class="doxyComputerOutput">Lg</span> removes the trailing zeros, so starting at <span class="doxyComputerOutput">LDBL_DIG</span> does not lose it. For zero and the subnormal values, which have fewer significant digits, the precision starts at 1. The value of <span class="doxyComputerOutput">errno</span>, which <span class="doxyComputerOutput">strtold</span> may set for subnormal values, is preserved. If no precision reads back exactly, the C library handles <span class="doxyComputerOutput">long double</span> with the precision of <span class="doxyComputerOutput">double</span> (e.g. newlib on AArch64 and RISC-V), and the value is cast to <span class="doxyComputerOutput">double</span> and formatted with <span class="doxyComputerOutput">std::to_chars</span>, as above.</li>
</ul>

<p>For all other numeric types, <span class="doxyComputerOutput">std::to_chars</span> is called directly, providing locale-independent formatting. The <span class="doxyComputerOutput">snprintf()</span> path uses the decimal point of the C locale, which is <span class="doxyComputerOutput">.</span> unless the application changes it with <span class="doxyComputerOutput">setlocale()</span>.</p>

<div class="doxyMemberDoc">

<p>Appends the hexadecimal address of a pointer to a buffer.</p>


<p>Shared by the <span class="doxyComputerOutput"><a href="/micro-test-plus-xpack/docs/api/classes/micro-os-plus/micro-test-plus/detail/reporter">reporter</a></span> and the <span class="doxyComputerOutput"><a href="/micro-test-plus-xpack/docs/api/classes/micro-os-plus/micro-test-plus/detail/expression-formatter">expression_formatter</a></span>, so that the pointers are displayed identically in the messages and in the expressions. Pointers to <span class="doxyComputerOutput">const</span> or <span class="doxyComputerOutput">volatile</span> objects, and function pointers, are accepted too.</p>

<p>Null pointers are rendered as <span class="doxyComputerOutput">"0x0"</span>, regardless of the platform, avoiding platform-specific representations such as <span class="doxyComputerOutput">"(nil)"</span> on Linux/glibc. Non-null pointers are formatted with <span class="doxyComputerOutput">snprintf()</span>, using the <span class="doxyComputerOutput">p</span> specifier.</p>


<p>The <span class="doxyComputerOutput">p</span> specifier expects a <span class="doxyComputerOutput">void*</span>. Object pointers are converted implicitly to <span class="doxyComputerOutput">const volatile void*</span>, which accepts any qualification, and the qualifiers are then removed with <span class="doxyComputerOutput">const_cast</span>; a <span class="doxyComputerOutput">reinterpret_cast</span> to <span class="doxyComputerOutput">void*</span> would not compile for pointers to <span class="doxyComputerOutput">const</span> objects. The object is not accessed. Function pointers, which do not convert to <span class="doxyComputerOutput">void*</span> implicitly, use <span class="doxyComputerOutput">reinterpret_cast</span>.</p>

<div class="doxyMemberDoc">

<p>Prepares an operand of a comparator.</p>


<p>The arrays and the pointers of the character types (<span class="doxyComputerOutput">char</span>, <span class="doxyComputerOutput">wchar_t</span>, <span class="doxyComputerOutput">char8_t</span>, <span class="doxyComputerOutput">char16_t</span>, and <span class="doxyComputerOutput">char32_t</span>, but not <span class="doxyComputerOutput">signed char</span> or <span class="doxyComputerOutput">unsigned char</span>, which are byte buffers) are converted to <span class="doxyComputerOutput"><a href="/micro-test-plus-xpack/docs/api/structs/micro-os-plus/micro-test-plus/detail/basic-c-string">basic_c_string</a></span>, so that they are compared by content; the other arrays, including those of <span class="doxyComputerOutput">volatile</span> characters, are converted to <span class="doxyComputerOutput"><a href="/micro-test-plus-xpack/docs/api/structs/micro-os-plus/micro-test-plus/detail/array-operand">array_operand</a></span>, so that they are compared element by element, the functions to function pointers, and all other operands are returned unchanged, so the other pointers, including the pointers to <span class="doxyComputerOutput">volatile</span> characters, and the functions are compared by address.</p>


<p>The other operands are forwarded, so that the comparator moves a temporary, and refers to a named operand.</p>

<dt class="doxyParamsTableTitle">Template Parameters</dt>
<dd>

</tr>
</table>
</dd>
</dl>

<dl class="doxySectionUser">
<dt>Returns</dt>
<dd><p>A <span class="doxyComputerOutput"><a href="/micro-test-plus-xpack/docs/api/structs/micro-os-plus/micro-test-plus/detail/basic-c-string">basic_c_string</a></span> for the C strings, an <span class="doxyComputerOutput"><a href="/micro-test-plus-xpack/docs/api/structs/micro-os-plus/micro-test-plus/detail/array-operand">array_operand</a></span> for the other arrays, otherwise <span class="doxyComputerOutput">t</span>, forwarded.</p></dd>
</dl>


<p>Arrays of the character types are converted using their size as a bound, pointers to them using the null terminator; the <span class="doxyComputerOutput">const</span> qualifier of the characters is ignored. The <span class="doxyComputerOutput">volatile</span> characters are not strings, since <span class="doxyComputerOutput"><a href="/micro-test-plus-xpack/docs/api/structs/micro-os-plus/micro-test-plus/detail/basic-c-string">basic_c_string</a></span> cannot refer to them: an array of them is converted to <span class="doxyComputerOutput"><a href="/micro-test-plus-xpack/docs/api/structs/micro-os-plus/micro-test-plus/detail/array-operand">array_operand</a></span>, like the other arrays, and compared element by element, and a pointer to them is forwarded, and compared by address, like the other pointers. The functions are converted to function pointers. Every other operand is forwarded, unchanged, as an lvalue or an rvalue reference.</p>


<p>The qualifiers of an array are those of its elements, so the element type is taken from the type of the argument, not from the type without qualifiers, which would lose the <span class="doxyComputerOutput">volatile</span> of the elements, and the conversion to the pointer to <span class="doxyComputerOutput">const</span> elements would not compile.</p>

### bind\_callable() {#a6abb44ef8226b1f80aad8010b5ef1a5c}

<div class="doxyMemberItem">
<div class="doxyMemberProto">
<div class="doxyMemberTemplate">template &lt;typename Self_T, typename Callable_T, typename... Args_T&gt;</div>
<table class="doxyMemberLabels">
<tr class="doxyMemberLabels">
<td class="doxyMemberLabelsLeft">
<table class="doxyMemberName">
<tr>
<td class="doxyMemberName">auto micro_os_plus::micro_test_plus::detail::bind_callable (Callable_T &amp;&amp; callable, Args_T &amp;&amp;... arguments)</td>
</tr>
</table>
</td>
<td class="doxyMemberLabelsRight">
<span class="doxyMemberLabels">
<span class="doxyMemberLabel nodiscard">nodiscard</span>
</span>
</td>
</tr>
</table>
</div>
<div class="doxyMemberDoc">

<p>Creates the function object that holds the body of a test case or suite.</p>


<p>Without additional arguments, the callable already has the signature <span class="doxyComputerOutput">void (Self_T&amp;)</span>, and a copy of it is returned, without a wrapper.</p>


<p>Otherwise, a <span class="doxyComputerOutput"><a href="/micro-test-plus-xpack/docs/api/classes/micro-os-plus/micro-test-plus/detail/bound-callable">bound_callable</a></span> stores copies of the callable and of the arguments (decayed, as by <span class="doxyComputerOutput">auto</span>), since a suite may run after the caller's temporaries are gone; the callable receives the copies as non-<span class="doxyComputerOutput">const</span> lvalues. A reference parameter thus refers to the copy; to refer to the caller's object, pass a pointer, or <span class="doxyComputerOutput">std::ref()</span>, which converts to a <span class="doxyComputerOutput">T&amp;</span> parameter (an <span class="doxyComputerOutput">auto&amp;</span> parameter receives the <span class="doxyComputerOutput">std::reference_wrapper</span> itself).</p>


<p>The returned object holds a copy of the callable (decayed, as by <span class="doxyComputerOutput">auto</span>) when there are no additional arguments; otherwise it is a <span class="doxyComputerOutput"><a href="/micro-test-plus-xpack/docs/api/classes/micro-os-plus/micro-test-plus/detail/bound-callable">bound_callable</a></span> that holds copies of the callable and of the arguments, and passes the arguments after the leading reference, which is passed when the body is invoked. No memory is allocated, other than by the copies themselves.</p>


<p>A suite stores the object in a <span class="doxyComputerOutput">std::function</span>, since it runs later; a test case, which runs immediately, refers to it with a <span class="doxyComputerOutput"><a href="/micro-test-plus-xpack/docs/api/classes/micro-os-plus/micro-test-plus/detail/callable-ref">callable_ref</a></span>.</p>

The operand types are deduced as forwarding references, prepared by <span class="doxyComputerOutput"><a href="#a51e86043001b197561806d5c6297041b">as_operand()</a></span>, and stored as <span class="doxyComputerOutput"><a href="#ae9fe49cb0d38724533e9a27a2232bf09">stored_operand_t</a></span> selects.</p>

### differ\_by\_at\_most() {#ad3e5817bc88a8b60b769b39a5fefee94}

<div class="doxyMemberItem">
<div class="doxyMemberProto">
<div class="doxyMemberTemplate">template &lt;class Lhs_T, class Rhs_T, class Epsilon_T&gt;</div>

</td>
<td class="doxyMemberLabelsRight">

<div class="doxyMemberDoc">

<p>Tells whether two numbers differ by at most a tolerance.</p>


<p>If the three values are integers, the distance is computed exactly, as an unsigned value, also for operands of mixed signedness, and compared with the tolerance with <span class="doxyComputerOutput">std::cmp_less_equal()</span>, so that neither overflows nor wraps around. Otherwise, the values are converted to their common floating-point type, and the absolute value of the difference is compared with the tolerance. A negative tolerance, or a NaN, makes the result <span class="doxyComputerOutput">false</span>.</p>


<dl class="doxyParamsList">
<dt class="doxyParamsTableTitle">Template Parameters</dt>

<table class="doxyParamsTable">

</tr>
<tr class="doxyParamItem">
<td class="doxyParamItemName">Rhs_T</td>

</tr>
<tr class="doxyParamItem">
<td class="doxyParamItemName">Epsilon_T</td>
<td class="doxyParamItemDescription"><p>The arithmetic type of the tolerance.</p></td>
</tr>
</table>
</dd>
</dl>

<dl class="doxyParamsList">
<dt class="doxyParamsTableTitle">Parameters</dt>
<dd>
<table class="doxyParamsTable">
<tr class="doxyParamItem">
<td class="doxyParamItemName">lhs</td>

</tr>

</tr>

<td class="doxyParamItemName">epsilon</td>

</tr>
</table>
</dd>
</dl>

<dl class="doxyParamsList">
<dt class="doxyParamsTableTitle">Return Values</dt>
<dd>
<table class="doxyParamsTable">
<tr class="doxyParamItem">
<td class="doxyParamItemName">true</td>
<td class="doxyParamItemDescription"><p>The distance between the values is less than or equal to the tolerance.</p></td>
</tr>
<tr class="doxyParamItem">
<td class="doxyParamItemName">false</td>
<td class="doxyParamItemDescription"><p>Otherwise.</p></td>
</tr>
</table>
</dd>
</dl>

<p>For the integers, the larger value is selected with <span class="doxyComputerOutput">std::cmp_less()</span>, and the distance is computed in <span class="doxyComputerOutput">std::uintmax_t</span>: when both values have the same sign, as the modular difference of their conversions, which is exact; otherwise, as the sum of the larger value and of the magnitude of the negative one. A sum that does not fit in <span class="doxyComputerOutput">std::uintmax_t</span> is flagged as an overflow, and gives <span class="doxyComputerOutput">false</span>, since the true distance is larger than any tolerance. The tolerance is compared with <span class="doxyComputerOutput">std::cmp_less_equal()</span>, so a negative one gives <span class="doxyComputerOutput">false</span>.</p>


<p>For the other types, the values are converted to their common type, which is a floating-point one, so <span class="doxyComputerOutput">std::int64_t</span> values compared with a <span class="doxyComputerOutput">float</span> tolerance lose precision; the comparison is inclusive, so a distance equal to the tolerance succeeds. Two equal values, including two infinities of the same sign, whose difference would be NaN, are at the distance zero; a NaN operand always fails.</p>

<div class="doxyMemberDoc">

<p>Escapes the control characters of a name.</p>


<p>Replaces, in place, the control characters other than the tab, including the line feed and the NUL, with their escape sequences, so that the names reach the console and the output files as one line of visible text. Defined in <span class="doxyComputerOutput"><a href="/micro-test-plus-xpack/docs/api/files/src/test-cpp">src/test.cpp</a></span>.</p>


<dl class="doxyParamsList">
<dt class="doxyParamsTableTitle">Parameters</dt>
<dd>
<table class="doxyParamsTable">
<tr class="doxyParamItem">
<td class="doxyParamItemName">name</td>
<td class="doxyParamItemDescription"><p>The name to escape.</p></td>
</tr>
</table>
</dd>
</dl>

<p>The text is scanned first, so that a name without control characters is not touched. The tab is kept; all the other control characters, including the line feed and the NUL, and DEL, are replaced.</p>

<div class="doxyMemberDoc">

<p>Reads the system clock.</p>


<p>Isolates the platform-specific access to the system clock, used by <span class="doxyComputerOutput"><a href="/micro-test-plus-xpack/docs/api/classes/micro-os-plus/micro-test-plus/detail/stopwatch">stopwatch</a></span> and by the deprecated <span class="doxyComputerOutput"><a href="/micro-test-plus-xpack/docs/api/classes/micro-os-plus/micro-test-plus/detail/timestamp">timestamp</a></span> class. The clock is monotonic on POSIX; without a clock, <span class="doxyComputerOutput">ts</span> is left unchanged, so the callers clear it first when a zero value must mean that the clock was not read.</p>


<dl class="doxyParamsList">
<dt class="doxyParamsTableTitle">Parameters</dt>

</table>
</dd>

<dl class="doxySectionUser">
<dt>Returns</dt>
<dd><p>Nothing.</p></dd>
</dl>


<p>On Windows, the current time is captured via <span class="doxyComputerOutput">timespec_get()</span> with <span class="doxyComputerOutput">TIME_UTC</span>. On POSIX platforms with <span class="doxyComputerOutput">CLOCK_MONOTONIC</span> defined, <span class="doxyComputerOutput">clock_gettime(CLOCK_MONOTONIC)</span> is used to obtain a monotonic reading. On platforms where neither macro is defined, <span class="doxyComputerOutput">ts</span> is left unchanged.</p>

<p>Always fails the static assertion that applies, since it is called only when <span class="doxyComputerOutput"><a href="/micro-test-plus-xpack/docs/api/concepts/micro-os-plus/micro-test-plus/extension/compare-tag">extension::compare_tag</a></span> is not satisfied: the missing or unprintable <span class="doxyComputerOutput">symbol</span> is reported first, then the <span class="doxyComputerOutput">apply()</span> that cannot be called with the operands, or whose result is not convertible to <span class="doxyComputerOutput">bool</span>.</p>

### reject\_comparison() {#a767a45bfc1b9f58e87b03e2e7698ffc5}

<div class="doxyMemberItem">
<div class="doxyMemberProto">
<div class="doxyMemberTemplate">template &lt;comparison Op, class Lhs_T, class Rhs_T&gt;</div>
<table class="doxyMemberLabels">

<div class="doxyMemberDoc">

<p>Stops the compilation of a comparator whose operands are rejected, with a message that tells why.</p>


<p>Always fails the static assertion that applies, since it is called only when <span class="doxyComputerOutput"><a href="/micro-test-plus-xpack/docs/api/concepts/micro-os-plus/micro-test-plus/detail/comparable-operands">comparable_operands</a></span> is not satisfied: an operand that cannot be written is reported first, then the operator that the operands do not support. Called by the overloads of the comparators that accept the rejected operands, so that the compiler shows this message instead of a list of the unsatisfied constraints.</p>

<p>Stops the compilation of a <span class="doxyComputerOutput"><a href="/micro-test-plus-xpack/docs/api/structs/micro-os-plus/micro-test-plus/detail/predicate-op">predicate_op</a></span> whose tag is rejected, with a message that tells why.</p>

### test\_each\_value() {#a3178150c77ae33d100e18e157436b04b}

<div class="doxyMemberItem">
<div class="doxyMemberProto">
<div class="doxyMemberTemplate">template &lt;class Self_T, class Values_T, class Callable_T&gt;</div>

<tr>
<td class="doxyMemberName">void micro_os_plus::micro_test_plus::detail::test_each_value (Self_T &amp; self, const <a href="/micro-test-plus-xpack/docs/api/classes/micro-os-plus/micro-test-plus/located-name">located_name</a> &amp; name, Values_T &amp;&amp; values, Callable_T &amp; callable)</td>
</tr>
</table>
</td>
</tr>
</table>

<div class="doxyMemberDoc">

<p>Adds and runs a test case for each value.</p>


<p>For each value, the name is built in a local string, which lives while the test case runs, since a test case runs within the call to <span class="doxyComputerOutput">test()</span>, and the test case is added with <span class="doxyComputerOutput">test()</span>, with the location of the call to <span class="doxyComputerOutput">test_each()</span>. The callable receives each value as a <span class="doxyComputerOutput">const</span> lvalue, referring to the element itself; neither the values nor the callable are copied. The values of a range are iterated by a range-based <span class="doxyComputerOutput">for</span> statement, and those of a tuple are expanded by <span class="doxyComputerOutput">std::apply()</span>, in order.</p>


<p>The common implementation of <span class="doxyComputerOutput"><a href="/micro-test-plus-xpack/docs/api/classes/micro-os-plus/micro-test-plus/test-case/#a419000e72526d0d251d7e28f48d656d2">test_case::test_each()</a></span> and <span class="doxyComputerOutput"><a href="/micro-test-plus-xpack/docs/api/classes/micro-os-plus/micro-test-plus/suite/#a61a886b526fef82564a3e4ec1ea0dee4">suite::test_each()</a></span>.</p>

### unwrap() {#a59eb53c96f68d26635c13df53b358ac8}

<div class="doxyMemberDoc">

<p>Returns the value wrapped by a framework type, or the operand itself.</p>


<p>Always call it qualified, as <span class="doxyComputerOutput"><a href="#a59eb53c96f68d26635c13df53b358ac8">detail::unwrap()</a></span>, so that argument-dependent lookup cannot select a function of the application, defined in the namespace of an operand.</p>


<p>The operand is returned by reference, without a copy; the result is valid only as long as the operand.</p>


<dl class="doxyParamsList">
<dt class="doxyParamsTableTitle">Template Parameters</dt>
<dd>
<table class="doxyParamsTable">
<tr class="doxyParamItem">
<td class="doxyParamItemName">T</td>
<td class="doxyParamItemDescription"><p>The type of the operand.</p></td>
</tr>
</table>
</dd>
</dl>

<dl class="doxyParamsList">
<dt class="doxyParamsTableTitle">Parameters</dt>
<dd>
<table class="doxyParamsTable">
<tr class="doxyParamItem">
<td class="doxyParamItemName">t</td>
<td class="doxyParamItemDescription"><p>The operand.</p></td>
</tr>
</table>
</dd>
</dl>

<dl class="doxySectionUser">
<dt>Returns</dt>
<dd><p>The value returned by <span class="doxyComputerOutput">t.get()</span> for the framework wrappers (the literals and the <span class="doxyComputerOutput">to_*</span> wrappers), otherwise a reference to <span class="doxyComputerOutput">t</span>.</p></dd>
</dl>


<p>If the type <span class="doxyComputerOutput">T</span> is a framework type (see <span class="doxyComputerOutput"><a href="/micro-test-plus-xpack/docs/api/concepts/micro-os-plus/micro-test-plus/extension/is-op">extension::is_op</a></span>) that provides a <span class="doxyComputerOutput">get()</span> member function, it is invoked and its result returned. Otherwise a reference to the argument itself is returned, so that the types of the application, even those with a <span class="doxyComputerOutput">get()</span> member function, are compared with their own operators, without a copy. The selection is performed at compile time via <span class="doxyComputerOutput">if constexpr</span> with an inline <span class="doxyComputerOutput">requires</span> expression; the return type is deduced with <span class="doxyComputerOutput">decltype (auto)</span> from the selected branch.</p>

<p>If the type <span class="doxyComputerOutput">T</span> is a framework type (see <span class="doxyComputerOutput"><a href="/micro-test-plus-xpack/docs/api/concepts/micro-os-plus/micro-test-plus/extension/is-op">extension::is_op</a></span>) that provides a <span class="doxyComputerOutput">get()</span> member function, it is invoked and its result returned. Otherwise a reference to the argument itself is returned, so that the types of the application, even those with a <span class="doxyComputerOutput">get()</span> member function, are compared with their own operators, without a copy. The selection is performed at compile time via <span class="doxyComputerOutput">if constexpr</span> with an inline <span class="doxyComputerOutput">requires</span> expression; the return type is deduced with <span class="doxyComputerOutput">decltype (auto)</span> from the selected branch.</p>


<p>Always call it qualified, as <span class="doxyComputerOutput"><a href="#a59eb53c96f68d26635c13df53b358ac8">detail::unwrap()</a></span>, so that argument-dependent lookup cannot select a function of the application, defined in the namespace of an operand.</p>


<p>The operand is returned by reference, without a copy; the result is valid only as long as the operand.</p>
